1.1.1.plain: Images, icons and other non-text content have a text description; decorative ones are hidden from screen readers.
1.1.1.question: Do images have text descriptions?

1.2.1.plain: Recorded audio-only content has a transcript; silent video has a text or audio version.
1.2.1.question: Do audio and silent videos have alternatives?

1.2.2.plain: Recorded videos with sound have captions for speech and important sounds.
1.2.2.question: Do videos have captions?

1.2.3.plain: Recorded videos have audio description or a full text version of what is shown.
1.2.3.question: Is what videos show described?

1.2.4.plain: Live video and audio broadcasts have live captions.
1.2.4.question: Do live broadcasts have captions?

1.2.5.plain: Recorded videos have audio description of important visual details.
1.2.5.question: Do videos have audio description?

1.2.6.plain: Recorded videos with sound have sign language interpretation.
1.2.6.question: Do videos have sign language?

1.2.7.plain: Where pauses are too short for description, the video pauses to allow extended audio description.
1.2.7.question: Is extended audio description available?

1.2.8.plain: Recorded video has a full text version that covers both sound and picture.
1.2.8.question: Do videos have a full text version?

1.2.9.plain: Live audio-only content has a live text alternative.
1.2.9.question: Does live audio have a text version?

1.3.1.plain: Headings, lists, tables and form groups are built so software can read the same structure people see.
1.3.1.question: Can software read the page structure?

1.3.2.plain: When the order of content matters, software reads it in that same order.
1.3.2.question: Is content read in a sensible order?

1.3.3.plain: Instructions do not rely only on shape, colour, size, position or sound.
1.3.3.question: Do instructions work without seeing shapes?

1.3.4.plain: The site works in both portrait and landscape, unless one orientation is essential.
1.3.4.question: Does it work in both orientations?

1.3.5.plain: Fields asking for personal details say what they are for, so browsers can fill them in.
1.3.5.question: Can browsers fill in personal details?

1.3.6.plain: The purpose of buttons, icons and regions is readable by software, so people can adapt them.
1.3.6.question: Can software tell what parts are for?

1.4.1.plain: Colour is never the only way information, actions or errors are shown.
1.4.1.question: Is colour the only signal anywhere?

1.4.2.plain: Sound that plays by itself for over 3 seconds can be paused, stopped or turned down.
1.4.2.question: Can automatic sound be stopped?

1.4.3.plain: Text stands out clearly from its background: contrast at least 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text.
1.4.3.question: Is text easy to see against its background?

1.4.4.plain: Text can be enlarged to 200% without losing content or features.
1.4.4.question: Can text be enlarged to 200%?

1.4.5.plain: Real text is used instead of pictures of text, except for logos or where it is essential.
1.4.5.question: Is text real text, not pictures?

1.4.6.plain: Text has enhanced contrast: at least 7:1, or 4.5:1 for large text.
1.4.6.question: Does text have very strong contrast?

1.4.7.plain: Recorded speech has no background sound, or the background is very quiet or can be turned off.
1.4.7.question: Is background sound quiet enough?

1.4.8.plain: Long text can be shown with chosen colours, short lines, good spacing and no full justification.
1.4.8.question: Can reading layout be adjusted?

1.4.9.plain: Pictures of text are used only for decoration or where the exact look is essential.
1.4.9.question: Are pictures of text avoided?

1.4.10.plain: At 400% zoom or 320 pixels wide, everything still works without scrolling sideways.
1.4.10.question: Does the page fit a narrow screen?

1.4.11.plain: Buttons, form fields, focus highlights and meaningful graphics have contrast of at least 3:1.
1.4.11.question: Are controls and graphics easy to see?

1.4.12.plain: Nothing is cut off or overlaps when people increase line, letter, word or paragraph spacing.
1.4.12.question: Does text survive wider spacing?

1.4.13.plain: Pop-up text shown on hover or focus can be dismissed, hovered over, and stays until moved away.
1.4.13.question: Can hover pop-ups be controlled?

2.1.1.plain: Everything can be done with a keyboard alone, without timed key presses.
2.1.1.question: Does everything work with a keyboard?

2.1.2.plain: Keyboard users can always move away from any part of the page.
2.1.2.question: Can keyboard users always move on?

2.1.3.plain: Everything can be done with a keyboard, with no exceptions.
2.1.3.question: Does every feature work by keyboard?

2.1.4.plain: Single-key shortcuts can be turned off or changed, or work only when their control is active.
2.1.4.question: Can single-key shortcuts be switched off?

2.2.1.plain: Time limits can be turned off, extended, or are long enough, with a warning before time runs out.
2.2.1.question: Can people get more time?

2.2.2.plain: Moving, blinking, scrolling or auto-updating content can be paused, stopped or hidden.
2.2.2.question: Can moving content be paused?

2.2.3.plain: Timing is not part of any task, except live events and video.
2.2.3.question: Is the site free of time limits?

2.2.4.plain: Interruptions such as updates and alerts can be postponed or turned off, except emergencies.
2.2.4.question: Can interruptions be postponed?

2.2.5.plain: After signing in again, people continue where they were without losing what they entered.
2.2.5.question: Is work kept after signing in again?

2.2.6.plain: People are told how long they can be inactive before they lose their data.
2.2.6.question: Are inactivity limits explained?

2.3.1.plain: Nothing flashes more than 3 times a second, unless the flashes are small and dim enough.
2.3.1.question: Is there dangerous flashing?

2.3.2.plain: Nothing flashes more than 3 times in any second.
2.3.2.question: Is there any fast flashing?

2.3.3.plain: Animation triggered by scrolling or clicking can be turned off, unless it is essential.
2.3.3.question: Can motion animation be turned off?

2.4.1.plain: There is a way to skip blocks repeated on every page, such as the main menu.
2.4.1.question: Can people skip repeated menus?

2.4.2.plain: Each page has a title that says what the page is about.
2.4.2.question: Do pages have clear titles?

2.4.3.plain: The keyboard moves through the page in an order that keeps meaning and makes sense.
2.4.3.question: Does the keyboard order make sense?

2.4.4.plain: Each link's purpose is clear from its text, or from its text with the surrounding sentence.
2.4.4.question: Is it clear where links go?

2.4.5.plain: There is more than one way to find a page, such as a menu, search or site map.
2.4.5.question: Are there several ways to find pages?

2.4.6.plain: Headings and labels describe the topic or purpose of what follows.
2.4.6.question: Are headings and labels descriptive?

2.4.7.plain: Keyboard users can always see where they are on the page.
2.4.7.question: Is the keyboard highlight visible?

2.4.8.plain: People can tell where they are within the site, for example with breadcrumbs.
2.4.8.question: Can people tell where they are?

2.4.9.plain: Each link's purpose is clear from the link text alone.
2.4.9.question: Is every link clear on its own?

2.4.10.plain: Sections of content are organised with headings.
2.4.10.question: Is content divided by headings?

2.4.11.plain: The keyboard position is never completely hidden by sticky headers, banners or pop-ups.
2.4.11.question: Is the keyboard position ever hidden?

2.4.12.plain: No part of the item with the keyboard position is hidden by other content.
2.4.12.question: Is the keyboard position fully visible?

2.4.13.plain: The keyboard highlight is large and contrasting enough: at least 2 pixels thick and 3:1 contrast.
2.4.13.question: Is the keyboard highlight strong enough?

2.5.1.plain: Actions that need swipes, pinches or paths can also be done with a single tap or click.
2.5.1.question: Do gestures have a simple tap alternative?

2.5.2.plain: Actions happen on release, so people can slide away to cancel an accidental press.
2.5.2.question: Can accidental clicks be cancelled?

2.5.3.plain: The name software reads out for a control includes the words shown on it.
2.5.3.question: Do control names match their visible text?

2.5.4.plain: Features triggered by shaking or tilting also have a button, and motion can be switched off.
2.5.4.question: Do motion features have a button?

2.5.5.plain: Clickable areas are at least 44 by 44 pixels, with limited exceptions.
2.5.5.question: Are tap areas large (44 px)?

2.5.6.plain: People can switch freely between input methods such as touch, mouse and keyboard.
2.5.6.question: Can people mix input methods?

2.5.7.plain: Anything done by dragging can also be done with single clicks or taps.
2.5.7.question: Does dragging have a click alternative?

2.5.8.plain: Clickable areas are at least 24 by 24 pixels, or spaced far enough apart.
2.5.8.question: Are tap areas big enough?

3.1.1.plain: The page states its main language, so screen readers pronounce words correctly.
3.1.1.question: Is the page language set?

3.1.2.plain: Passages in another language are marked, so they are pronounced correctly.
3.1.2.question: Are other-language passages marked?

3.1.3.plain: Unusual words, idioms and jargon have their meaning available.
3.1.3.question: Are unusual words explained?

3.1.4.plain: Abbreviations have their full form or meaning available.
3.1.4.question: Are abbreviations explained?

3.1.5.plain: Text that needs more than lower secondary reading level has a simpler version or summary.
3.1.5.question: Is there a simpler version of complex text?

3.1.6.plain: Where pronunciation changes meaning, the correct pronunciation is available.
3.1.6.question: Is ambiguous pronunciation explained?

3.2.1.plain: Moving the keyboard position to something does not by itself open pages or change the context.
3.2.1.question: Does focusing something trigger surprises?

3.2.2.plain: Changing a setting or field does not open pages or submit forms without warning.
3.2.2.question: Do fields trigger unexpected changes?

3.2.3.plain: Menus and navigation repeated across pages appear in the same order every time.
3.2.3.question: Is navigation consistent across pages?

3.2.4.plain: Things that do the same job are named and labelled the same way across the site.
3.2.4.question: Are the same things named consistently?

3.2.5.plain: Big changes such as new windows happen only when people ask for them.
3.2.5.question: Do changes happen only on request?

3.2.6.plain: Help such as contact details or chat appears in the same place on every page.
3.2.6.question: Is help always in the same place?

3.3.1.plain: When a form detects a mistake, it points to the field and describes the error in text.
3.3.1.question: Are form errors identified in text?

3.3.2.plain: Form fields have labels or instructions that say what to enter.
3.3.2.question: Do form fields have clear labels?

3.3.3.plain: When a form knows how to fix a mistake, it suggests the correction.
3.3.3.question: Do error messages suggest a fix?

3.3.4.plain: Legal, financial and data submissions can be reversed, checked or reviewed before they are final.
3.3.4.question: Can important submissions be checked first?

3.3.5.plain: Context-sensitive help is available where people fill in information.
3.3.5.question: Is help available while filling forms?

3.3.6.plain: Any form submission can be reversed, checked or reviewed before it is final.
3.3.6.question: Can every submission be checked first?

3.3.7.plain: Information already given in the same process is filled in or offered, not asked for again.
3.3.7.question: Do people have to retype information?

3.3.8.plain: Signing in does not require remembering, transcribing or solving puzzles without an easier option.
3.3.8.question: Can people sign in without puzzles?

3.3.9.plain: Signing in never requires recognising objects or personal content, or solving puzzles, without an alternative.
3.3.9.question: Is sign-in free of any memory test?

4.1.2.plain: Every control has a name, a type and a state that software can read and that update when they change.
4.1.2.question: Can software read every control?

4.1.3.plain: Messages such as 'Added to cart' or search result counts are announced without moving the keyboard position.
4.1.3.question: Are status messages announced?
